dependency_simplification:
DRIFT / REUSE
Searched for existing list scheduling, native sequencing, bank reversal,
reflection and rotation interfaces. Existing SequentialFive is for disjoint
banks, whereas these stages share the same live bank; the existing public
clock/append compiler already provides the required mechanism. Used it
without inventing a new machine model. The list proof is a direct induction
on actual stage schedules and result_spec. Raw IO, initial encoding, native
prefix/halt refinement and state counts are all reused. The original
stateBits_div_tendsto remains the sole asymptotic input; its small wrapper
is now shared by two executors, removing the duplicated R1881 proof body.
All head algebra is built from existing append_position, scan positions,
physical erase/rewind, original run and frozen halt. The shifted stage
approximants reuse processing_curve_shift_covers, bank/scratchCurve_error,
clippedRamp_sample_error/start_error, ticks_bounds, bankPosition_error and
scratchPosition_bounds. No new compactness or block-rounding framework.
The compiled word is a foundation for the mixed source206 palette. A full
forward-only exclusion must not be mistaken for the required theorem with
backward scans, reversals, rotations and row/integer/F3 operations. Next
extend the concrete instruction palette, reusing/generalizing this word
compiler, and assemble bounded finite-family covers for the mixed words.
No matching bank-reversal/rotation executor was found in the targeted search;
existing copy/absolute-tape routines should be reused when constructing it.
